[[A]]

Assistant A provides a clearer, more accurate, and more accessible explanation tailored to a non-technical audience. It correctly identifies that language models are typically trained on unlabeled data via self-supervised learning, explains what "unlabeled" means in plain language, and describes how the model learns patterns from raw text. Assistant B is technically imprecise by stating models "can be trained using either labeled or unlabeled data" without clarifying that standard pre-training relies on unlabeled data, and its response is too brief to build understanding or trust.
